issue: P1 (WP6; decisive fixed-shape ranking experiment declared in phase_plan section 11 item 1)

shapes.geometry_binding: analytic; occupancy cell-center mask + watertight anchor STL sharing one geometry_id (re-voxelized IoU = 1.0 for every shape)

experiment_setup.stage_t: same-grid T1 (60x32x24, voxel 0.05), alphaMax 2500, q=0 identity on binary fields; primal-converged, no transfer operator, no filter/projection, no optimizer

resolvability_rule: I_f > 2 * max(S_b, S_c, S_extraction) with the declared band (Gate 4, docs/problem_resolution_plan_2026_09.md section 7)
measured_findings: Downforce ranking (raw values, maximize sense): V1 'unresolved' (zero resolvable sign inversions, rho 0.9394); V2 'no_go' with exactly one resolvable sign inversion: plate_a20_nd vs plate_a20_t05 (surrogate says the thicker plate is better by +0.2316, the qualified body-fitted reference says the thinner plate is better by +0.0343, just above 2x the declared band 0.0294).

The thickness cluster itself (a20_nd 0.15 m, t10 0.10 m, t05 0.05 m) plateaus in the body-fitted reference (V2 differences 0.014-0.034 around the declared band) while the surrogate separates them by up to 0.23: the surrogate over-rewards thickness-driven downforce.
Drag: 37/37 resolvable pairs have AGREEING signs at both V1 and V2 (rho 0.976, tau 0.911); verdict 'unresolved' only because adjacent order swaps inside the near-noise cluster are sub-threshold.

Extraction block (E): iso 0.50 reproduces the anchor within 0.0013 downforce; thresholds 0.45/0.55 shift downforce by -0.030/+0.013; extraction error is of the same order as the declared band, which is why the ranking uses analytic anchors.

alphaMax block: 250 vs 2500 changes per-shape forces by <=8% (DF plate_a20_nd -0.4881 vs -0.5297), solid-band leakage 1-2% vs 0.1-0.2%, and the force share from beta<0.1 cells is ~1e-6: P11-era saturation behavior is confirmed for binary fixed shapes; no haze.

verdict_by_response.downforce: no_go (per pre-registered Gate-4 rule at V2; the inversion is a real, geometry-clean factor: thickness)
verdict_by_response.drag: unresolved_ranking_consistent (sign-consistent everywhere resolvable; order swaps only inside the sub-threshold cluster)

claims_supported: For binary, same-grid, transfer-free, extraction-free, fixed operating-point geometry: the fixed-grid Brinkman surrogate PRESERVES the fine-fidelity ordering for 37/37 resolvable drag pairs and for the large downforce-magnitude structure (AoA series, span, z-offset, sign control), and MISRANKS the thickness subset of downforce by a resolvable margin (rho 0.879-0.939, tau 0.733-0.822).
The no_go is response- and factor-specific (downforce x thickness axis), not a global invalidation of the surrogate.
claims_not_supported: No grid-independent downforce claim; the declared band 0.0129-0.0147 remains, unresolved.
No claim that any other surrogate or formulation would rank correctly.

No claim that the t-cluster reference ordering is grid-independent (its differences are 0.014-0.034, straddling the declared band); the direction is consistent across V1 and V2 but only resolvable at V2.
